method: Qiling emulation + bit-precise shadow memory; stdin tainted at read(), taint checked at every guest write into canary_after
notes: flags all 20 OOB stride-4 stores value-tainted -- an OVER-TAINT. The taint is the len control byte, NOT attacker register data (clearing len -> 0 tainted; clearing all 80 register bytes -> still 20). It is laundered by two imprecisions: mov reg<-mem does not clear stale register taint, so len's taint from the loop-bound computation survives into the untainted loop index; then loading through that spuriously-tainted address taints the value (pointer-avalanche). Sound (never misses the write) but imprecise.
